relevance_note: The paper describes two cousins in a six-patient CRMO series with LPIN2 mutations: 'Two patients underwent genetic studies and were found to have LPIN2 mutation'.
method_note: Read by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. Tables 1-4 are headings only in the Markdown (no table content), so all per-patient data in Tables 1 and 2 (including the LPIN2 variant descriptions) are unavailable; variant rows are kept with variant_original_string 'not reported'. Two in-scope people: the index case/proband (no own label; role words are not labels, so 'unnamed person 1') and his cousin ('cousin of unnamed person 1'), who 'shared the same LPIN2 mutation'. The other four CRMO patients have no LPIN2 variant reported and get no rows (cohort_size_as_stated = 6). Group statements naming all 6 patients ('all were boys', 'Tibia and fibula were involved in all the patients', '6 patients were diagnosed as CRMO', 'All patients were initially treated with ... NSAIDs ... and methotrexate') were applied to both. Counts without names (low grade fever 2/6, ESR elevated in all except one, bone involvement 4/6 or 1/6, bone biopsy in two children) were not assigned. 'Rest of the patients had isolated bone disease' was recorded only as excluded 'extra osseous manifestation' for the cousin; no narrower checklist item was excluded from it. 'Anemia with leucopenia' was not mapped to microcytic anemia or neutropenia. The etanercept sentence was assigned to the index case because it directly follows the index-case sentence and precedes 'The second patient'. The intro sentence 'The authors have described 2 patients from the same family ... 4' and 'Two of the patients in our series were diagnosed as Majeed syndrome with LPIN2 mutation in our study.4' were read as a prior report of the same two patients (ref 4); country 'Indian subcontinent' comes from that intro sentence. Zygosity and inheritance are not stated (only that Majeed syndrome is autosomal recessive in general). No contradictions found.

span: All patients were initially treated with on nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and methotrexate.

The index case diagnosed to have Majeed syndrome responded partially to a combination of 3 monthly pamidronate with methotrexate and required intermittent NSAIDs for control of symptoms with frequent flares.
TNF α blocker (etanercept biosimilar) was used intermittently (due to financial constraints) to control the flare on a weekly basis on 2 occasions a year apart.

span: One patient with anemia with leucopenia and was subjected to a bone marrow examination, which revealed congenital dyserythropoietic anemia (later diagnosed as Majeed syndrome)
Two patients underwent genetic studies and were found to have LPIN2 mutation

The diagnosis of CRMO was based on the history of insidious onset of bone pain and/or swelling and presence of radiologic evidence of multiple osteolytic lesions in the long bones/bone biopsies showing sterile chronic inflammation.
